nexusClaim.associationBasis: The Christensen 2016 long-term follow-up of primary repair for chronic thumb ulnar collateral ligament injuries documents some degree of osteoarthritis in 88% of evaluated patients at a mean 24.5 years after repair of injuries greater than six weeks old, with increased age at injury and higher DASH scores correlating with increased radiographic grades, the Daley 2020 review characterizes chronic collateral ligament injuries of the thumb MCP joint as a distinct management entity, and the Fairhurst 2002 series documents ongoing MCP joint pain in two of 22 reconstructed gamekeeper's thumbs; the literature documents post-traumatic degeneration at the chronically injured joint without establishing that a gamekeeper's thumb caused an individual's osteoarthritis.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: The mapping does not assert that gamekeeper's thumb caused an individual's osteoarthritis: the 88% figure derives from a 12-patient long-term subset of surgically treated chronic injuries with selection and survivorship bias, no natural-history cohort follows untreated chronic UCL insufficiency to incident radiographic osteoarthritis, primary first carpometacarpal (basal) thumb osteoarthritis is far more common and occurs at a different joint, prior MCP fracture or dislocation and inflammatory or crystal arthropathy independently produce MCP degeneration, and degeneration may predate or accompany the ligament injury; individual claims require documented chronic UCL injury predating documented osteoarthritis at the injured MCP joint with alternative joint and inflammatory causes excluded.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized chronic-instability contact-stress pathway: an incompletely healed or reconstructed ulnar collateral ligament leaves the thumb metacarpophalangeal joint with persistent valgus laxity, so pinch and grip load drives the proximal phalanx into excessive valgus and lateral translation with each grasp cycle; the altered joint kinematics redistribute contact stress onto the ulnar and dorsal cartilage surfaces, producing cumulative microtrauma, cartilage matrix breakdown, and subchondral remodeling that conventional radiographs capture as post-traumatic osteoarthritis - the same instability-to-degeneration logic the acl-injury and ankle-strain osteoarthritis edges carry - while the pathway remains a hypothesis about an individual's course because no cohort quantifies progression from chronic UCL insufficiency to incident osteoarthritis.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Following the acl-injury and ankle-strain osteoarthritis precedents, the edge asserts an association only: the outcome evidence is a 12-patient long-term radiographic subset of surgically treated chronic injuries plus narrative reviews and a 22-thumb reconstruction series, no untreated natural-history cohort quantifies progression, the operated cohort is selected for symptomatic chronic instability, and primary basal-thumb osteoarthritis, prior fracture, and inflammatory arthropathy independently produce thumb-joint degeneration; no probability estimate is asserted.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Documented chronic thumb UCL injury (valgus stress testing, radiocarpal/MCP ultrasound or MRI) with injury date; osteoarthritis documented at the same MCP joint (radiographic joint-space narrowing, osteophytes, subchondral changes) with onset chronology after the ligament injury; exclusion of primary first carpometacarpal basal-thumb osteoarthritis, prior MCP fracture or dislocation, inflammatory or crystal arthropathy, and ligament reconstruction complications; hand-surgery or orthopedic assessment of the individual relationship
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Primary first carpometacarpal (basal) thumb osteoarthritis at a different joint
Rheumatoid, psoriatic, or crystal arthropathy of the MCP joint
Concomitant acute skier's-thumb injury or Stener lesion with its own course
Age-related degeneration unrelated to the ligament injury

suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY following the post-traumatic osteoarthritis precedents for ligament and strain injuries: long-term radiographic follow-up documents degeneration at the chronically injured MCP joint while selection bias, absent natural-history data, and the far more common primary basal-thumb alternative defeat individual causal attribution, so the mapping asserts the association with joint-level, chronology, and alternative-cause requirements.
